newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe sees Q4 gold production increase.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe sees Q4 gold production increase.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp said Wednesday it expects a marked increase in gold production beginning in the fourth quarter.
The company said it is confident it will meet goals to produce more than 1.0 million ounces in 1997 and 1.25 million ounces in 1998.
The company said production will increase as production at its Lone Tree Mine Section 14, Trenton Canyon and the new Sage Mill at the Twin Creeks Mine begin.

Ramp-up of production will continue into 1997, the company said, with added gold production from Mule Canyon, Twin Creeks, Lone Tree and the Rosebud joint venture. The company said all these new projects "are proceeding on or ahead of schedule and within budget."
The company reported Wednesday that third quarter earnings had fallen to $0.03 per share from $0.07 a year-ago.

It said gold production was 204,708 ounces in the third quarter, up from 198,514 ounces in the third quarter 1995. It reported year-to-date production of 594,452 ounces, compared to 631,805 ounces in 1995.
